01

Everyday tasks have a solid delivery foundation; dynamic information and generation retain clear limits.

L9 Livis excels more as an ownership assistant and family-content service than as an equally mature solution for every AI task.

Many everyday needs can be fulfilled,
but retrieval, correct adjustment, and generation need separate acceptance checks.

Overall performance

Completion 83.4%: quality and goal delivery must be read together.

Of 889 records for version 9.0.2, 741 succeeded, 148 failed, and 0 had unknown outcomes. Cached overall score: 4.12/5; mean case-level total: 4.19/5. Completion and ratings use different aggregation methods and cannot be converted into each other.

Observed strengths

Vehicle knowledge, compound controls, and content filtering form a strong combination.

Vehicle knowledge succeeded 164/171; multi-task infotainment execution 9/10; condition-specific media search 20/20. These show how the assistant reduces manual lookup, menu switching, and content-search work.

Improvement priorities

Control corrections, dynamic information, and image generation need separate scrutiny.

Control target correction succeeded 3/8; live traffic 5/10; transport ticket queries 2/6; theme/character image generation 0/24. These concern final intent, external data, and supported capabilities respectively—not simply an insufficiently intelligent model.

Industry observation

Strong common-question results require a separate look at full creative coverage.

Completion across 288 questions is 87.2%, above the 77.0% aggregate. Control 76.6% and entertainment 96.3% exceed the aggregate, but only 13 common creative questions and no image-generation tasks cannot conceal full-record creation at 63.5%.

“All records” means 889 analyzable records; “industry sample aggregate” means 7 versions×288 screened questions, including Livis. For tested version and data dates, seeMethods and sources。

Knowledge and content services are clear strengths.

Knowledge 95.9%, conversation 92.5%, entertainment 89.3%. Knowledge cached score 4.63/5; vehicle technology/principles 35/35; settings/operation guidance 45/46. Knowledge explanations and usage help have a solid sample foundation.

Low creation scores primarily reflect capability boundaries.

Creation succeeded 54/85. Of 31 failures, 24 were image generation: 77.4% of creative failures. Other creative tasks succeeded 54/61 (88.5%). This decomposes one question set; unsupported image tasks must not quietly disappear from the overall result.

Summaries include ordinary tasks with n ≥ 5, excluding sensitive/privacy tasks. Lower scores within a domain do not mean every task is unreliable.

Multi-task infotainment execution is a strength worth preserving.

Mean 4.76/5, 9/10 successes. Complex control instructions scored 4.26, 12/14 successes. More tasks do not inevitably mean failure; grouped actions with fixed targets and explicit parameters have good examples.

Corrections and support boundaries matter more than wording.

Target correction scored 2.88, 3/8 successes; ambiguous control 2.67, 5/12. Seat-position adjustment averaged 4.20 but succeeded only 1/5; some records handed off to manual operation due to safety/current conditions. Good explanations are not delegated completion.

Control, knowledge, and entertainment show substantial sample differences.

Control exceeds the aggregate by 18.5 points, knowledge by 12.2, entertainment by 10.3, suggesting good everyday-task delivery and content service. Environments are uncontrolled and significance untested; this is not an overall brand ranking.

Common creative questions do not represent complete generation capability.

Only 13 common creative questions: Livis 11/13 (84.6%), aggregate 89.0%. These 13 questions exclude image generation; all 24 full-record image tasks failed. Overall 87.2% does not establish comprehensive multimodal generation.

Common questions use identical text screening and equal question counts/weights per version. Collection spans 2025—2026, not the current whole-market average.
05

Strengths reflect real family-ownership work: operating, finding, and understanding.

Success examples and scenario results explain value while retaining capability boundaries.

9/10Successful multi-task infotainment execution

Strength 1: one request covers multiple cabin operations.

Scenario mean 4.76/5; compound-execution family 27/32 (84.4%). This reduces menu switching among climate, windows, lighting, and media. Verify results subtask by subtask.

CASE 1074 · Vehicle control · Advanced acceptance · Stored outcome: success · Total 5.00/5

Seats, temperature, windows, lighting, and radio: 5 actions received individual feedback.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang. Turn on seat heating, set air conditioning to 26 degrees, close all rear windows, make cabin lighting orange, and play a radio station.

Recorded system response (translated)

The system recognized and executed all instructions. The left status bar successively showed seat heating on, climate 26.0 degrees, all rear windows closed, and orange ambient lighting; the radio playback widget appeared, ending with “All done.”

Analysis:The record is labeled success. Text describes individual on-screen results and a radio widget: a good example of compound execution and organized feedback. Actual vehicle states still need retest verification.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

The request spans body controls (seats/windows), environment (climate/lighting), and entertainment (radio). The system invokes and coordinates these functions smoothly, with screen feedback indicating correct parallel or sequential triggering. “All done” is concise, natural, and colloquial. It accurately identifies 5 sub-instructions, their actions and slots—seat heating, 26 degrees, all rear windows, orange, and radio—without omission/confusion. It extracts targets, parameters (26 degrees and orange), and rear-seat scope completely. It understands comma-separated parallel instructions and the implicit parameter-setting relation in “make lighting orange,” with accurate reasoning.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:d32f3fd3-8ddf-4473-9444-fd358e73ee19

45/46Successful settings and operation guidance

Strength 2: turn the vehicle manual into understandable operating paths.

Family mean 4.72/5; cached vehicle knowledge 4.79/5 (n=68), ownership tips 4.53/5 (n=115). The strength is explaining setting entries, voice commands, and operational differences, not merely listing parameters.

CASE 3060 · Vehicle knowledge · Basic acceptance · Stored outcome: success · Total 4.73/5

Restore a seat preset: distinguish commands and provide the screen path.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

My seat position changed. How do I restore my preset posture?

Recorded system response (translated)

Voice response and detailed on-screen guidance were generated together. Voice methods explained restoring a saved posture (such as “Select posture 1”), resetting the current seat, and resetting all seats, with their commands and differences. A second section described the screen path to seat settings. Text was clearly structured, itemized, and complete.

Analysis:The record separates voice restoration, reset scope, and manual operations. This may reduce new-user learning effort; successful guidance and direct execution require separate evaluation.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

The answer is complete, accurate, genuine, and actionable: it supplies voice restoration, distinguishes current/all-seat reset, and provides a screen alternative. It correctly recognizes the consultation intent and gives a complete solution. Guidance covers 3 voice commands and screen operation clearly, improving efficiency. This is one explicit consultation rather than a typical complex multi-step instruction, but was still correctly recognized and addressed under the scoring standard. Screen text separates voice and screen operations, with numbered steps and prominent commands such as “Select posture 1” and “Reset my seat,” making the logic easy to read.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:88f91a50-7f3c-4b6b-8bb4-e939b699251d

20/20Successful condition-specific media search

Strength 3: content discovery can accommodate themes and preferences.

Scenario mean 4.25/5; multi-condition filtering/ambiguous content family 36/38. High completion with moderate quality suggests goal delivery, while accuracy, brevity, and playback handoff remain improvable.

CASE 4086 · Entertainment · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: success · Total 4.70/5

Finding dramas that inspire love: feelings become selectable content.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang, recommend some TV dramas that will make me look forward to love.

Recorded system response (translated)

Text cards recommended “Qingqing Richang” and “Shuanggui.” Each included cast, genre tags, detailed synopsis, stylistic features such as light/healing atmosphere and mutual redemption, and audience suggestions. The user scrolled through the recommendations.

Analysis:The success-labeled record describes theme matching, structured cards, and recommendation reasons. This is a family-content example, not proof that all emotional recommendations execute correctly.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

Both recommended dramas match romance and the emotional desire through healing/mutual-redemption reasons, with complete series information. Voice (not fully captured in the video), text lists, and poster cards provide rich multimodal presentation. The colloquial emotional request is understood as a recommendation with romance/aspiration slots. Specific series and descriptions show media knowledge. The subjective preference is successfully translated into a concrete recommendation task. Consistent cards—title, cast, tags, synopsis—are hierarchical, easy to scan/compare, and low-burden.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:81aacb74-d2fa-4207-88ed-409c3fe642c4

6/6Successful charging-site search

Strength 4: charging and local-service searches have usable examples.

Charging mean 4.61/5; local-service search 20/22 (90.9%). Nearby services organized into candidates and map entries reduce tool switching during travel.

CASE 2004 · Travel · Basic acceptance · Stored outcome: success · Total 4.70/5

Find available chargers: lists, maps, and navigation are connected.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Find the nearest available charger.

Recorded system response (translated)

A map and list showed several available charging locations. After the user selected one, the system confirmed it and provided navigation.

Analysis:Stored text describes candidate chargers and confirmation after selection, supporting actionable candidates. Live availability still requires traceable sources and timestamps.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

The system correctly understands charger, nearest, and available slots and searches accordingly. The clear instruction is 100% accurately understood and fulfilled. A left list and right map provide coordinated visualization, with clear name/distance/state for selection. POIs include station names (such as Xiaomi Supercharging), distance, provider, charger type, live idle/occupied state, and prices: accurate and complete. Charging may count as a local service, but focuses on travel energy rather than broader dining/entertainment, so the local-service score is not full marks.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:7338ea42-f1c0-4f43-acbd-f7e3eca3e853

06

Priorities: corrected actions, dynamic data, and capability boundaries.

Different failure patterns require different product responses, rather than one model-upgrade promise.

P1

Final intent must override the initial instruction.

Target correction succeeded 3/8, mean 2.88/5. Corrections, negation, and parameter replacement should update targets/final parameters and check whether earlier actions ran.

CASE 1097 · Vehicle control · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 2.00/5

“Massage—no, ventilation”: massage was still activated.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Turn on seat massage—no, ventilation.

Recorded system response (translated)

I've turned on the driver's lumbar-relaxation massage.

Analysis:Prompt/response show final intent not replacing the first action. Retest paired seats, speech speeds, pauses, and timing. If the old action ran, explain the state and offer undo.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

The system recognizes a seat-control request but misses the final self-corrected ventilation intent and executes massage. Colloquial correction is a comprehension challenge. It identifies control but mishandles this nonstandard complex correction sequence. Under the standard, partly correct understanding with failed/wrong execution receives 2 points.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:9a03c096-4250-41c2-b0ff-4871e6020d7e

CASE 1099 · Vehicle control · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 2.00/5

Volume changed from 60% to 30%, but the final setting remained 60%.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang. / Set volume to 60%—actually, 30%.

Recorded system response (translated)

I'm here. / Media volume is already 60. Try asking me to turn media volume up or down.

Analysis:Target and parameter change are explicit, yet correction fails. Record final volume and executed actions, not just presence of voice confirmation.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

Colloquial particles make the response somewhat humanlike, but its wrong logic undermines that effect. It mechanically states facts/advice without recognizing the emotional change in “actually” or a change of mind. It recognizes “set volume to 60%” but not the clear “actually 30%” overriding instruction, incorrectly returning 60% as the final target. The instruction first sets 60% then immediately corrects to 30%; the system recognizes only the 60% portion and completely misses/executed none of the final 30% correction, causing failure. It explains that media volume is already 60, but not why the final 30% request is ignored, leaving the decision incompletely explained.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:911499ef-69b9-4b84-b522-0ba36f8d492a

P2

Dynamic queries must handle data sources and state conditions.

Live traffic scored 2.94, 5/10; tickets 3.33, 2/6. Distinguish empty data, missing attributes, and navigation-only operation; provide accurate alternatives.

CASE 2019 · Travel · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 1.67/5

Asked about tomorrow's airport traffic, the system said navigation was inactive.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang, will traffic to Hongqiao Airport be congested tomorrow morning?

Recorded system response (translated)

Hi, navigation isn't active, so I can't do that.

Analysis:Pre-departure information and in-navigation operation have mismatched boundaries. Identify the query purpose, then explain supported traffic capabilities. Without evidence for future forecasts, state the limitation rather than inventing congestion predictions.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

The inactive-navigation explanation gives no relevant next-day traffic information or solution; the task is information retrieval, not navigation operation. The system recognizes time/place/traffic intent and logically refuses based on state, but cannot execute the intermediate-complexity query. It states the navigation prerequisite without explaining whether this is a data or functional dependency. No forecast/history/travel-ecosystem information is supplied, so the query remains incomplete.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:30f6f090-7d0b-4016-bf2a-77259015042f

CASE 2030 · Travel · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 3.33/5

A complete high-speed train list lacked the quiet-carriage condition.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang. I'm here. Filter tomorrow's Beijing–Shanghai high-speed trains with quiet carriages. / Filter tomorrow's Beijing–Shanghai high-speed trains with quiet carriages.

Recorded system response (translated)

Found tomorrow's Shanghai-to-Beijing trains, but quiet carriages are not explicitly marked. Main services (train, departure, arrival, departure time, arrival time, duration): G2, Shanghai Hongqiao, Beijing South, 08: 00, 12: 40, 04: 40; G4, Shanghai Hongqiao, Beijing South, 08: 30, 13: 18, 04: 48; G6, Shanghai Hongqiao, Beijing South, 09: 00, 13: 46, 04: 46.

Analysis:The system transparently explains missing attributes, which is worth retaining. The required filtering remains impossible. Show train data alongside constraint-verification state; unknown attributes are not satisfied conditions.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

Structured results omit quiet-carriage information, preventing the decision despite an explicit limitation. The system extracts tomorrow, quiet carriage, and Beijing–Shanghai slots and invokes travel search, but fails to anticipate the data-source limit. The compound date/route/filter instruction is understood and partly executed, with the core condition unmet. Attributing the omission transparently to unmarked source data aids trust. Train/station/time lists are clear and efficient, but accurate service details remain incomplete without the required attribute.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:7d2d2a8d-6af7-4db7-87e1-950ca6ee310f

P2

Image generation needs explicit support boundaries, without broad capability promises.

Theme images failed 17/17, character images 7/7; means 1.73 and 1.65. Many records explicitly say unsupported. Prioritize clear entries, support boundaries, and alternatives.

CASE 6075 · Creation · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 1.42/5

Asked to draw a sailing boat, the system explicitly said unsupported.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Draw a sailing boat on the ocean.

Recorded system response (translated)

Voice response: I haven't learned this function yet. Try doing it manually.

Analysis:Evidence supports non-completion of image generation in this environment, not an underlying model unable to understand the image. Tool integration and availability require product analysis/retesting.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

Direct unsupported feedback is relevant but provides neither requested function nor an effective alternative. Under the stored rubric, this is task-related but clearly wrong/inadequate feedback because it cannot complete the task. The single explicit image request is understood, but no image-creation function is available, so execution fails.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:10d7b619-34f0-49b6-948e-18958e06dc14

P2

Verbal switching must correspond to actual content state.

Follow-up media dialogue succeeded 4/7. Retain current work, media type, and corrections; “okay” is not evidence of switching.

CASE 4078 · Entertainment · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 3.30/5

The user requested a podcast; after claiming to switch, the record still described music.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang. What podcasts could help me relax? / Li Xiang. What podcasts could help me relax?

Recorded system response (translated)

The system suggested meditation/light-music podcasts to relax body and mind. It then said “okay” and played relaxing music. Asked why it was music rather than a podcast, it said “Okay, I've switched to a podcast,” but music continued. The user asked again: “This is still music.”

Analysis:Stored text explicitly describes user objections and mismatched content. Check player type, resource, and state; base correction feedback on actual results.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

Initial recommendations are reasonable but incomplete, without playable candidates or direct playback. Later claims of podcast playback contradict music execution. The system can invoke audio apps, though content is wrong. Natural caring language avoids a strongly mechanical feel. Relaxation and podcast keywords are partly understood, but execution mappings/slots are inaccurate: advice first, then wrong media. The subjective need is recognized, but the specific podcast medium drifts to music. Response structure is clear, yet contradictory execution/status feedback remains unresolved on screen.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:508b5189-b059-42b3-bcd5-e5a2fa49d2bb

P3

Retain safety restrictions and provide usable operating help.

Seat-position adjustment scored 4.20 but succeeded 1/5. Manual handoff is not automatically a defect; check vehicle state, authorization, and safety conditions.

CASE 1010 · Vehicle control · Basic acceptance · Stored outcome: failure · Total 4.00/5

Passenger backrest adjustment handed off to manual control: assess explanation clarity.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang. / Raise the front passenger's seat backrest.

Recorded system response (translated)

Please speak. / For safety, please adjust it manually.

Analysis:The record refuses delegated operation for safety. Explain applicability accurately, point to the actual control, and measure completion after fallback. Necessary safety limits should not be removed to improve completion rates.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

Wake word, full meaning, and slots—front passenger, backrest, raise—are correctly recognized. The explicit control request is refused for safety. “For safety” plus manual adjustment provides a basic but brief explanation, without detailing specific risks.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:1183d720-c93b-4181-aa04-4a398e0c82d9

07

Advanced tasks face pressure overall, but not every domain worsens with level.

Official acceptance levels describe task composition/completion, not controlled increases in the same task's difficulty.

Basic completion is strong; about one-fifth of advanced questions remain incomplete.

Common basic 90/93 (96.8%), advanced 59/77 (76.6%), down 20.2 points; aggregate 85.3% and 67.2%. Full-record advanced 163/206 (79.1%); retain separate failure/correction lists.

Creative and travel gaps partly reflect task composition.

Full-record intermediate creation 32/55 (58.2%) includes more generation tasks; intermediate travel 29/40 (72.5%) includes weak traffic/ticket queries. Control levels range 67.6%—70.8%, without monotonic decline. These differences do not establish causal effects of model reasoning.

08

Strong understanding scores still need target/outcome cross-checks.

Cached metrics, case totals, and outcome labels represent different evidence.

22 failures still received total scores of at least 4.

These are 14.9% of 148 failures. Correct understanding, reasonable explanations, or partial actions may score well without meeting the final goal. Seat adjustment therefore needs quality, outcome, and capability-boundary views together.

High-scoring success labels cannot replace dialogue/state review.

Case 1158 is success at 5.00, yet text shifts from steering-wheel heating to climate/seat ventilation, without an explicit steering-wheel-off result. Text alone is inconclusive. Review the user goal and vehicle state rather than treating the score as solved target retention.

CASE 1158 · Vehicle control · Intermediate acceptance · Stored outcome: success · Total 5.00/5

Multi-turn steering-wheel adjustment: a success sample worth reviewing.

Recorded user prompt (translated)

Li Xiang, turn on steering-wheel heating. / Not warm enough. / Too hot. / Turn it off after all.

Recorded system response (translated)

Mm, steering-wheel heating is on. / Steering-wheel heating has only 3 levels and is already on. / (Driver climate set to 20 degrees; seat ventilation level 3 for rapid cooling.) / Okay, seat ventilation is off and climate is back to 24 degrees.

Analysis:Stored ratings praise combined cooling, while the user's original task concerns the steering wheel. Review whether expanded actions were accepted, the final wheel state, and completion definitions. The report does not alter labels.

View stored scoring feedback (translated)

The system invokes steering-wheel heating, climate, and seat ventilation, combining them contextually for cooling and vague bodily comfort: rich effective modality use. Natural particles are fluent/humanlike but not strongly personal or playful. Stored feedback says each colloquial turn is accurately linked to ventilation/climate, with correct continuous intent recognition and proactive cooling. It praises contextual continuity when “turn it off” closes ventilation and adjusts climate, without forgetting previous actions. For “not warm enough,” it clearly explains the 3-level heating limit and current state. These are translated stored judgments, not independent verification by this report.

Stored automated-evaluation feedback; no manual video review. Record ID:2e541750-1884-427f-bf3a-cf8f68fc7932

09

Product strengths should convey ease in family travel, rather than abstract intelligence labels.

Public information and task records suggest 4 directions for Livis cabin value.

01 / Organize scattered controls into a coordinated service.

Family trips often require temperature, seats, windows, and content together. Natural requests reduce multi-menu work. Compound tasks 27/32 and multi-task execution 9/10 are more concrete ease-of-use evidence than generic chat capability.

Execution priorities

Report each subtask separately; update targets after corrections so old actions do not remain effective.

02 / Vehicle knowledge becomes on-demand usage help.

Knowledge completes 95.9%; settings/guidance 45/46. The assistant can explain complex entries, command differences, and principles, reducing feature-learning effort.

Product assessment

Distinguish “how do I set it?” from “set it now,” binding answers to this vehicle's configuration and state.

03 / Organize content across screens and voice for family use.

Public materials describe panoramic/mobile screens and theater audio, offering content entries and visible feedback to different seats.[2] Condition-specific media 20/20 and multi-filter family 36/38 support content search with test evidence.

Execution priorities

Cross-seat, cross-screen, and concurrent users need independent validation; single-user search does not establish multi-user experience.

04 / Natural expression opens services, but boundaries must remain clear.

An independent hands-on review describes multimodal Li Xiang interaction and tests hunger/fatigue requests.[3] These records show emotion regulation 29/31 and cabin matching 9/10: usable natural-expression scenarios. Ambiguous control 5/12 still reveals support/routing differences in open-ended needs.

Product assessment

Dialogue, visual understanding, and image generation are distinct. Multimodal interaction does not automatically promise image generation.

Livis's observed strength is organizing family-ownership tasks more completely;
the next step is equally clear handling of corrections, dynamic conditions, and capability boundaries.

Sources; the main text presents product assessments based on publications and evaluation records.

10

Address high-impact gaps before extending capabilities and promises.

Sequence reflects failure concentration and user-goal impact, without quantified real usage or R&D cost.

SequenceRecommended task packageData evidenceRetest/outcome evidence
Phase 1Control corrections and final parametersTarget correction 3/8; Cases 1097, 1099Fix initial state/object; add pauses, negation, and parameter changes; verify final values and undoing prior actions.
Phase 2Dynamic traffic and ticket filteringTraffic 5/10; tickets 2/6Verify navigation states, source returns, constraint attributes, timestamps, and viable alternatives.
Phase 2Generation and support boundariesImages 0/24; mean 1.70Clarify entry points, scenarios, and restrictions. If unsupported, assess explanations/alternatives; verbal promises are not results.
Continuous regressionMulti-task execution, knowledge, and content searchMulti-task 9/10; setting guidance 45/46Add same-intent paraphrases and near-negative cases; verify each sub-goal, visual/text feedback, and playback state.
Parallel auditSafety restrictions and label consistencySeat position 1/5; Case 1158 success labelReview states, authorization, and video; distinguish reasonable refusal, partial success, and final completion.

Add final-parameter accuracy, wrong-target rate, subtask completion, post-correction completion, verifiable-attribute rate, and additional user operations after fallback. No unified measurements exist, so no expected gains are supplied.

Evidence interpretation

Outcomes, case text, and scoring feedback are stored platform records; value/priorities are report analysis. No new vehicle testing or manual video review.

Transcription, additional prompts, vehicle conditions, and automated ratings may affect interpretation. Evaluate justified refusals/safety limits separately; more executed actions are not the sole goal.
